newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Dozens hurt by toxic leak at Russia nuclear plant.
newsitem.headline: Dozens hurt by toxic leak at Russia nuclear plant.

text.p: Forty-three people were taken to hospital after a leak of toxic material at a nuclear centre at Nizhny Novgorod, east of Moscow, Itar-tass news agency said on Monday.
It quoted local civil defence officials as saying that the accident occurred on Sunday when the toxic substance, cadmium dimethyl, leaked at a plant belonging to the Sarovo nuclear centre.
Emergencies Ministry spokeswoman Marina Ryklina was quoted as saying that a seal had failed on an air-tight line in one of the working rooms.

Fifteen of the 43 people admitted to hospital were diagnosed as having "slightly damaged upper respiratory tracts", the agency said. Officials were not immediately available for comment on the report, which gave no further details.

Environmental hazards are widespread in Russia, where communist-era central planning paid scant regard to the possible effects of pollution and today's authorities, struggling with an economic crisis, have few funds to spare on improving standards.

The international environmental group Greenpeace said on Monday that dangerous dioxins from chemical plants, factories and burning rubbish dumps were poisoning nearly three quarters of Russia, making it one of the world's most polluted countries.
